name: Spear
definition: shaft with a pointed head made for thrusting or throwing; yari and qiang are named forms.
notes: KoA Spears & Spearheads: 72 items, Han Sha, Assegai, Viking spear heads; yari not on page.

name: Halberd
definition: polearm combining an axe blade, a spike and a hook on one head.
notes: Cold Steel Man at Arms Swiss Halberd filed under Halberds; KoA lists Halberds (10).

name: Naginata
definition: Japanese polearm with a long curved single-edged blade.
notes: Hanwei Sohei Naginata: sharpened functional naginata, breadcrumb Spears Polearms.

name: Glaive
definition: polearm with a single-edged blade on the end of the shaft.
notes: KoA shop category Glaives & Bardiches (3 items); menu only, no product row read.

name: Battle axe
definition: axe made for fighting, not for cutting wood.
notes: Cold Steel Viking Battle Axe sold as a Norse battle axe under Axes.

name: Tomahawk
definition: light one-handed axe made for fighting or throwing.
notes: Cold Steel Hudson Bay tomahawk listed under Functional Weapons; page pitches camp use as well as collecting.

name: Bō staff
definition: long wooden staff used as a weapon.
notes: Cold Steel polypropylene training bo, octagonal Okinawan style, 137 cm.

name: Gun staff [棍]
definition: Chinese long staff weapon of the apparatus lists.
notes: AWMA guide names Gun Staff as a bo-like staff type in rattan; no product page for it.

name: Mace
definition: club with a heavy head, often flanged or spiked.
notes: Cold Steel MAA Gothic Mace, 28 in, flanged head.

name: War hammer
definition: hafted weapon with a hammer head, often backed by a spike.
notes: KoA category War Hammers (24) with Baltimore Knife & Sword and Tod Cutler items.

name: Baton
definition: rigid or telescoping club made for striking.
notes: ASP 26 in expandable Friction Loc baton; telescoping.

name: Tonfa
definition: baton with a side handle set at right angles to the shaft.
notes: AWMA tonfa category: wood, foam-covered and polypropylene training tonfas.

name: Nunchaku
definition: two short sticks joined by a cord or chain.
notes: AWMA Nunchaku & Nunchucks: 38 items, wood and foam, speedchucks.

name: Kubotan
definition: short rod held in the fist to strike or apply pressure.
notes: BladeHQ product type Kubaton: Cold Steel Delta Dart 8 in polymer; a reviewer calls it pointed.

name: Flail
definition: striking head joined to a handle by a chain.
notes: KoA category Flails (7); category count only, product rows not read.

name: Rope dart
definition: dart or blade on the end of a long rope, swung and cast.
notes: Century Martial Arts kung fu rope dart, 11 ft cotton rope, half-pound dart.

name: Chain whip
definition: jointed steel segments ending in a dart, swung as a whip.
notes: WLE steel 9-section wushu chain whip.

name: Three-section staff
definition: three staff sections joined end to end by chains or cords.
notes: Home of Poi sells sanjiegun as fire prop only; AWMA guide names sectional staff sansetsukon.

name: Pepper spray
definition: canister that sprays an irritant agent as a mist or stream.
notes: SABRE Red keychain pepper spray, stream pattern, 3-in-1 formula.

name: Pepper gel
definition: canister that sprays an irritant agent as a sticky gel.
notes: SABRE Red MK-9 gel delivery pepper spray, 16 oz, law-enforcement line.

name: Pepper-ball launcher
definition: launcher that fires frangible projectiles filled with an irritant powder.
notes: Byrna HD XL kit: launcher with pepper projectiles and 12 g CO2; same product as CO2 launcher.

name: CO2 launcher
definition: compact CO2-powered launcher made for self-defence projectiles; may merge with E4.7.03 when attested.
notes: Byrna SD fires .68 cal kinetic and irritant projectiles on 8 g CO2; same launcher as pepper-ball kind.

name: Projectile electroshock weapon
definition: device that fires wired darts to deliver an incapacitating electric shock; TASER is a maker-bound named form.
notes: TASER Pulse 2, Bolt 2, TASER 7 CQ, X1 fire two wired darts plus contact stun.

name: Contact stun gun
definition: hand-held device that delivers an electric shock through electrodes pressed against the body.
notes: Guard Dog Dual LED grip-to-stun gun ring; page does not describe electrodes.

name: Plate helmet
definition: metal helmet made against blows; burgonet is a named form.
notes: Deepeeka Burgonet helmet, 18 gauge steel, falling buffe; Armor > Helmets.

name: Ballistic helmet
definition: helmet made against bullets and fragments; `protection_level` is an attribute (E-23, provisional).
notes: Atomic Defense Ops-Core ballistic helmets: FAST SF, XP, XR, RF1, TBH; NIJ IIIA stated for some.

name: Soft ballistic vest
definition: flexible body armour against handgun rounds.
notes: Point Blank Hi-Lite Male concealable vest, NIJ 0101.06 Level II or IIIA.

name: Hard ballistic plate
definition: rigid armour plate against rifle rounds, worn alone or in a carrier.
notes: Spartan Armor Systems Hercules Level IV stand-alone ceramic plate, NIJ 0101.06.

name: Stab-resistant vest
definition: body armour made against knife and spike attacks (NIJ 0115.00).
notes: Protech Corrections Persuader stab vest, NIJ 0115.00 compliant; level not stated.

name: Plate carrier
definition: vest made to hold hard armour plates, armour in its own right (K-84).
notes: Atomic Defense plate carriers collection: QRF minimalist plate carrier with plates.

name: Gauntlet
definition: armoured glove protecting the hand and wrist.
notes: KoA Plate Gauntlets: 19 items (Maximilian, Churburg, hourglass, mittens).

name: Arm armour
definition: loose armour for the arm, such as vambrace and couter.
notes: KoA Plate Pauldrons & Arms (35): bracers, couters, arm armour sets.

name: Leg armour
definition: loose armour for the leg, such as greave and cuisse.
notes: KoA Plate Legs & Tassets (37): poleyns, greaves, cuisse and poleyn sets.

name: Plate armour harness
definition: complete suit of plate armour; a garniture is a named form.
notes: KoA category Full Suits of Armor (2) and Plate Armor Sets (8); counts only.

name: Shield
definition: hand-held protective barrier carried on the arm.
notes: Reliks Windlass Steelcrafts domed steel buckler under Shields; KoA menu lists round, heater, buckler.

name: Centrefire handgun cartridge
definition: complete cartridge with a central primer made for handguns.
notes: Sportsmans Handgun Ammo (959): 9mm Luger, .40 S&W, .45 Auto, .357 Magnum.

name: Centrefire rifle cartridge
definition: complete cartridge with a central primer made for rifles.
notes: Sportsmans Rifle Ammo (1,580): .308 Win, .223 Rem, 6.5 Creedmoor, 5.56mm NATO.

name: Rimfire cartridge
definition: complete cartridge whose priming compound sits in the rim.
notes: Sportsmans Rimfire Ammo (124): .22 LR, .22 WMR, .17 HMR.

name: Shotshell
definition: cartridge for a shotgun loaded with shot or a slug.
notes: Sportsmans Shotgun Ammo (973) by gauge 12, 20, .410, 28, 16, 10.

name: Muzzle-loading projectile
definition: ball or conical bullet loaded from the muzzle.
notes: Muzzle-Loaders.com: Hornady round balls, Great Plains and PA conicals, T/C Maxi-Ball.

name: Black powder and substitute propellant
definition: black powder and its substitutes for muzzle-loading arms (E4-O2).
notes: Hodgdon Pyrodex P, RS, Select sold as black powder substitute for muzzleloaders.

name: Air-gun pellet
definition: lead or alloy projectile made for air guns.
notes: Pyramyd Air pellets: 272 products, shapes domed, pointed, wadcutter, hollowpoint.

name: Arrow
definition: shafted projectile shot from a bow (E4-O1).
notes: Lancaster Archery: Easton 6.5mm Hunter Classic fletched hunting arrows.

name: Crossbow bolt
definition: short shafted projectile shot from a crossbow.
notes: Barnett Headhunter 20 in carbon crossbow bolts with lighted nocks.

name: Loose bullet
definition: projectile sold on its own for loading cartridges (K-86).
notes: Hornady ELD-X loose rifle bullets, 100 count, sold for reloading.

name: Primer
definition: ignition cap sold on its own for loading cartridges (K-86).
notes: Bass Pro Primers (32): CCI Benchrest large rifle, CCI small pistol magnum, Winchester 209.

name: Smokeless propellant powder
definition: smokeless powder sold for loading cartridges (K-86).
notes: Bass Pro Reloading Powder (35): Hodgdon H4350, Vihtavuori N135, Accurate No. 5.

name: Magazine
definition: detachable or fixed container that feeds cartridges into a firearm.
notes: EuroOptic Magpul PMAG magazines for AR15, AK, Glock, Scorpion.

name: Bowstring
definition: string made to fit a bow or crossbow.
notes: Lancaster and 3Rivers navigation list bowstring categories; string material page, not a finished string.

name: Arrow rest
definition: device on the bow riser that supports the arrow before release.
notes: Trophy Ridge Whisker Biscuit Pro arrow rest; Lancaster lists drop-away and blade rests.

name: Scabbard
definition: sheath made to hold a sword or knife.
notes: HanBon Forge replacement saya for katana, wakizashi, tanto.

name: Sword guard
definition: loose guard for a sword hilt; tsuba is a non-maker named form.
notes: Collectors Firearms tsuba category, 17 pages, signed Umetada pieces.

name: Grip ornament (menuki)
definition: loose ornament fitted under the grip wrapping of a Japanese sword.
notes: Collectors Firearms pair of menuki, shi-shi motif, category Menuki.

name: Rifle scope
definition: telescopic sight made to mount on a firearm, air rifle or crossbow.
notes: EuroOptic Vortex Viper PST Gen II 2-10x32 riflescope; only title and nav read.

name: Weapon light
definition: light made to mount on a weapon (K-162).
notes: Primary Arms Streamlight TLR-1 HL weapon light, rail mount.

name: Bipod
definition: two-legged support made to mount on a weapon (K-163).
notes: Optics Trade Caldwell Shooting Bipod, Sitting Model.

name: Shooting rest
definition: support on which a weapon is laid to steady the aim (K-163).
notes: Optics Trade Caldwell Rock BR competition front shooting rest.
